title: Harness Self-Evolution for Long-Horizon Terminal Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.27435v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Long-horizon terminal agents may solve a task in one run yet fail across repeated runs. Stochastic errors can propagate through actions and context, creating a gap between capability and reliable execution. We present RiseHarness, a framework for iteratively improving agent harnesses with model weights fixed. It focuses on flipping tasks with both successful and failed runs under the same configuration, using successful runs as references for failure analysis. RiseHarness combines agent trajectories with internal harness traces from a runtime monitor to examine how model actions interact with command execution, feedback, context management, and completion decisions. A Harness Handbook links this evidence to harness behaviors and source code, helping identify recurring problems in mechanisms shared across tasks. translated_title: 面向长时程终端智能体的Harness自演化框架
translated_abstract: 长时程终端智能体可能一次运行就能解决某个任务，但在多次重复运行中却可能失败。随机性错误会通过动作和上下文不断传播，造成模型能力与可靠执行之间的差距。我们提出了RiseHarness，一个在模型权重保持固定的情况下迭代改进智能体harness的框架。它专注于那些在同一配置下既有成功运行又有失败运行的任务，并将成功运行作为失败分析的参考。RiseHarness将智能体轨迹与来自运行时监控器的内部harness追踪记录相结合，以考察模型动作如何与命令执行、反馈、上下文管理和完成决策相互影响。一份Harness手册将这些证据与harness的行为和源代码关联起来，帮助识别跨任务共享机制中反复出现的问题。随后，RiseHarness会搜索其他harness框架中的相关实现，并将其改编为当前harness的设计参考。
tldr: RiseHarness提出了一种在模型权重固定的前提下，通过对比同一任务的成功与失败运行、结合智能体轨迹与运行时监控证据、并借鉴其他harness框架的实现来自演化迭代改进智能体harness的框架，从而弥合能力与可靠执行之间的差距。
en_tdlr: RiseHarness is a framework that iteratively self-evolves agent harnesses with frozen model weights by contrasting successful and failed runs of the same task, leveraging trajectory and runtime-monitor evidence along with a Harness Handbook, and adapting implementations from other harness frameworks to close the gap between capability and reliable execution in long-horizon terminal agents.
